title: The Tessl Agent: Build Your Software Factory on Autopilot
description:
What if your AI agent aimed to render itself unnecessary? The Tessl Agent does just that by setting up a self-sustaining software factory. It seamlessly drives automation deeper into your workflow, orchestrating tasks, and optimizing performance without demanding constant supervision. Imagine interacting with other coding agents and initiating recurring actions — it's not just about minor improvements, but efficiency that compounds, transforming coding into less toil and more shipping.

Dru Knox, Head of Product at Tessl, delves into the philosophy and engineering behind the Tessl Agent. He focuses on making tools that facilitate seamless scaling and smarter code reviews without the need for human redundancy. As the head of product development, Knox brings valuable insights into loop engineering, a method designed to automate feedback and evolve software practices over time.

What we cover:
• What is the Tessl Agent and how does it integrate with the Tessl platform?
• How does loop engineering drive automated feedback?
• How to set up an agentic code review environment
• Is optimizing your AI agent costs really the wrong lever?
• Why modular software factories are crucial to avoid vendor lock-in
• Why is outcome-oriented UX now the baseline in AI development?

Chapters:
00:00:00 - Introduction
00:02:00 - What is the Tessl agent?
00:05:00 - The Tessl agent and Claude Code: how it feels to use
00:06:24 - Setting up agentic code review: a walkthrough
00:12:24 - Loop engineering: the self-improving factory
00:17:00 - The two traps teams fall into with agents
00:18:24 - How loops solve the autonomy investment problem
00:21:01 - Thinking about agent cost: the right and wrong approaches
00:24:00 - Skills, context, and the open platform philosophy
00:29:35 - Why your factory should be modular — and why lock-in is dangerous
00:34:01 - How Tessl's skills platform and the agent connect
00:43:40 - UX in the AI era: outcome-oriented interfaces
00:46:24 - Other use cases: repo readiness, delegation, and more loops on loops
00:49:06 - What's next for the Tessl agent
